findings.finding: consequences defaulted differently between decision_log.md (missing-key default) and the seeded ADR spec file (falsy-value default) for a schema-valid empty-string consequences value.
findings.suggestion: Applied after PASS (cheap, matches established sha-normalization pattern): normalized once in _resolve_retroactive_adrs; both renderers now read the already-normalized value. Regression test: test_resolve_retroactive_adrs_normalizes_consequences_fallback.

findings.finding: test_generate_fails_closed_before_writing_claude_md duplicates ~20 LOC of git-init/snapshot fixture already in test_cross_links.py.
findings.suggestion: Deferred, explicitly non-blocking per reviewer: test_cross_links.py is not otherwise in this diff (never refactor an untouched file).

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: Step E's fail-closed ordering fix means nothing can abort after artifacts are already overwritten — _max_seeded_adr_number's _SEED_FILENAME_NUMBER_RE accepted 4-digit filename prefixes, matching shared/adr_index.py's own tolerance. A foreign year-prefixed file (e.g. 2019-choose-postgres.md) in the seed folder could inflate the computed max past ADR_OUTPUT_MAX_NUMBER, and that raise fires deep inside write_agent_docs, AFTER architecture.md/conventions.md are already overwritten.
findings.suggestion: FIXED: narrowed _SEED_FILENAME_NUMBER_RE from \d{3,4} to \d{3} — adopt only ever writes 3-digit names, so a 4-digit file can never collide with what adopt would pick, and counting it toward the max served no purpose beyond manufacturing a false overflow. The overflow check's own late-firing position is pre-existing (confirmed against the main tree, not introduced by this diff) and left as-is.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: INDEX.md is covered by adopt's existing output-safety machinery the same way every other artifact is — A successful _refresh_adr_index never entered results["written"] (only _seed_adr_spec_folder's paths did), so check_paths_against_gitignore never looked at it. A repo with INDEX.md gitignored would silently ship a seeded ADR folder with no index.
findings.suggestion: FIXED: write_agent_docs now appends the index path to `paths` (which feeds results["written"] and the gitignore check) on a successful refresh.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: AC1's 'INDEX.md must be regenerated' actually holds in the installs adopt ships to — _refresh_adr_index's best-effort failure (missing shared/ tree) surfaces as one stderr line nobody is instructed to read, and validate_adoption.py checked nothing about the ADR folder or its index.
findings.suggestion: FIXED: new soft_check_adr_seed_folder (in hollow_adr_detection.py) warns when the seed folder has no .md files, or has files but no INDEX.md.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: duplicating ADR_SPEC_FOLDER in adopt is the same safe pattern shared already uses — shared/tests/test_adr_index_producers.py pins the shared-side copies together; adopt's copy (forced to duplicate the string since importing adr_index.py trips ADR-045) was outside that test's reach entirely.
findings.suggestion: FIXED: new test_adr_spec_folder_agrees_with_shared_adr_index, a regex-based cross-check against shared/scripts/lib/adr_index.py's source (no import, no lib collision).

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the hollow_adr_detection extraction's file-location loader is as safe as the fixed shared_loader.py idiom — _hollow_adr_detection()'s loader lacked the missing-file-to-named-ImportError guard and the pop-sentinel-on-failing-exec guard that shared_loader.py documents for the shared/-tree case.
findings.suggestion: FIXED: added both guards, mirroring shared_loader.py's idiom. Regression test: test_hollow_adr_detection_loader_does_not_poison_cache_on_failure.
